Definition: a primary verb; to be used (by habit or conventionality); neuter perfect participle usage:--be custom (manner, wont).
BiblicalUsage: Éthō means to be accustomed — to do a thing as a matter of custom, the way you always have. Jesus went into the synagogue on the Sabbath 'as his custom was', and Paul reasoned in the synagogue three Sabbaths 'as his manner was'. The word is habit made visible.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe éthō shows me the shape of a faithful life: it is built out of customs kept week after week. Jesus and Paul both had a 'as his custom was', and I want one too.
